answer.line: Seven can win 1st, six are left for 2nd, five for 3rd: 7 x 6 x 5 = 210.

steps: Ask whether order matters. 1st, 2nd and 3rd are different awards, so the same three runners in a new order is a new result.
Fill the slots: 7 choices for 1st, 6 for 2nd, 5 for 3rd. Multiply: 7 x 6 x 5 = 210.
Check it with groups. 35 groups of three, each lined up 6 ways: 35 x 6 = 210.

choices.note: 6 is 3 x 2 x 1, the ways to line up three runners you already picked. It skips choosing which three of the seven.
21 counts the ways to give one runner one award: 7 x 3. A finish gives out all three awards from a shrinking pool: 7, then 6, then 5.
35 counts the groups of three when order does not matter. The awards differ, so each group lines up 6 ways.
7 x 7 x 7 lets one runner win two places. A runner who places leaves the pool.

lockIt: Different prizes mean order matters: multiply the shrinking pool. Same prize: divide out the orders.

playWith.label: Permutations vs Combinations: set n to 7 and r to 3, then switch from Permutation to Combination

groups.label: 35 stops at groups: which three placed, not in what order.
groups.ordersLabel: Each group lines up 3 x 2 x 1 = 6 ways: 35 x 6 = 210.

repeat.label: 7 x 7 x 7 = 343 would let one runner win twice.

visual.alt: Three slots for 1st, 2nd and 3rd, each showing the 7 runners as dots with one more greyed out per slot, so the choices read 7, 6 and 5. The product 7 x 6 x 5 = 210 is outlined. Notes below split 210 into 35 groups times 6 orders and show that 343 needs repeats.
visual.caption: Each award takes one runner out of the pool: 7, then 6, then 5.
